params.body:
## Why

A designed report arrives with its sources as the designers wrote them: a link straight to the publisher, or an address printed with no link. Every source in a report's list is held in Gentells and has its own page on gentells.com (`/sources/{key}`, #450), but the file that goes out never used those pages. Three reports with new covers are about to go to readers that way.

## What changes

- **`core/report-stamp.mjs`.** `stampReport(bytes, sources)` makes the outgoing file from the designers' file:
  - a link the designers made to a held source is pointed at that source's page (same page, with or without `www`, a closing slash or tracking parameters);
  - an address printed without a link gets one over the text, on the report's source pages, also when it wraps over several lines;
  - two sources that print the same address (two Eurostat pages as `ec.europa.eu/eurostat`) each get their own page, by the title beside it;
  - nothing else changes: no text, picture or page.
- **It names what it could not place.** A link that still leaves for another site, a held source whose address is not on a source page, and a held source without a page on gentells.com.
- **The designers' file is kept.** `store/report-releases/<slug>/original.pdf` is the file as uploaded; `report.pdf` is what goes out. The stamp is always made from the original, so it never stacks, and the source check keeps reading the addresses the designers wrote. A report stored before this change has only `report.pdf`: it becomes the original at the first stamp.
- **When it runs** (`core/report-links.mjs`):
  - on upload in the Studio (`POST /reports/:slug/file`); the answer carries `links`. A stamp that fails leaves the designers' file on the shelf and says so;
  - after `bin/cite-report-sources.mjs` holds a report's sources, and after its `--undo`;
  - `bin/stamp-reports.mjs [<slug> ...] [--dry]` for the reports already on the shelf.
- **`GET /reports/:slug/sources`** carries `links`: what the last stamp did.
- The report's fingerprint follows the outgoing file, so the site fetches it again. Page count and rendered previews stay as the upload made them.
- **New dependency: `pdf-lib`**, to write link annotations. `pdfjs-dist`, already here, reads where the text sits.

## Checked

- `test/report-stamp.test.mjs`: a report built in the test with a linked body, a centred source list, a repeated address and a wrapped one. Full suite 1712/1712, `tsc` clean.
- On the three designers' files: The New Status System 17 of 17 sources through Gentells (19 links repointed); Going Out, Staying In 11 of 11 held sources (2 repointed in the body, 11 added on the source page); Growing Up in Public 18 of 18 with stand-in keys (18 added). Every page of each file renders pixel for pixel as before.

## After the merge, on the box

```
node bin/stamp-reports.mjs --dry
node bin/stamp-reports.mjs
```

The first says per report what it would do and names every link that still leaves. A report uploaded after the merge is stamped on its own.

Closes #470
Closes #469 (the same request, opened twice)
params.title: Reports: source links go through Gentells in the file that goes out
